How Apple Watch Smart Stack works — and why listing copy is a separate job

Teams assume Smart Stack widget support in the watchOS binary covers storefront language. WidgetKit timelines, Smart Stack suggestion logic, and App Store Connect actually separate on-device Smart Stack behavior from product-page copy:

  • Smart Stack on the watch face — in watchOS 10 and later, a stack of glanceable widgets sits on the watch face. Users turn the Digital Crown to rotate widgets in and out. watchOS labels it 智能叠放 in Simplified Chinese. Does not generate Chinese listing text by itself.
  • Digital Crown rotation — the primary interaction: crown up or down cycles through stack widgets while the time remains visible. Gallery frames may show crown-turn demos or "Turn the Digital Crown" badges — listing copy should use 转动数码表冠 or Digital Crown 转动叠放 when that is what the screenshot depicts.
  • Glanceable widgets — weather, calendar, fitness, reminders, and third-party watch widgets appear as stack cards. Your description may list supported widget types; implementing WidgetKit timelines is engineering — distinct from zh-Hans caption lines.
  • Smart Stack suggestions — watchOS can suggest context-relevant widgets to pin or reorder in the stack. Listing copy covers screenshot caption lines about suggestions — not on-device suggestion algorithm engineering.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Smart Stack widgets in the binary.

Working Smart Stack widgets on Apple Watch and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other. AppLocale FAQ

What is Apple Watch Smart Stack and how do users interact with it?

Smart Stack is the rotating widget stack on the Apple Watch face in watchOS 10 and later. Users turn the Digital Crown to cycle glanceable widgets — weather, calendar, fitness, reminders, and third-party watch widgets — while the time stays visible. watchOS can suggest context-relevant widgets for the stack. Simplified Chinese watchOS labels it 智能叠放.

How is Smart Stack different from Watch complications?

Complications are individual slots embedded in a watch face layout — Corner, Graphic Circular, Modular — 表盘复杂功能. Smart Stack is a crown-driven widget carousel on the face — turn Digital Crown to cycle widgets — 智能叠放 / 表盘智能叠放. Same wrist, different marketing surface.

How is Smart Stack different from iPhone widgets, StandBy, and Watch Faces?

iPhone widgets use the Home Screen or Lock Screen Add Widget gallery — 主屏幕小组件. StandBy is iPhone landscape charging nightstand mode — 待机显示. Watch Face gallery is browsing clock face styles — 表盘图库. Smart Stack is wrist widget cycling with the Digital Crown — 智能叠放 — not phone widget galleries, not nightstand mode, and not face style collections.

How is Smart Stack different from Live Activities, Double Tap, and Mirroring?

Live Activities are time-bound iPhone updates — 实时活动. Double Tap is the wrist pinch gesture — 轻点两下. Mirroring shows the Watch screen on iPhone — 手表镜像. Smart Stack is crown-driven widget rotation on the watch face — 转动数码表冠 / 智能叠放.

Does a Smart Stack–aware watchOS app auto-translate my China listing?

No. WidgetKit timelines and in-app stack behavior control on-device surfacing — they do not create or fill a Simplified Chinese localization row. Empty or English zh-Hans fields mean China buyers see en-US fallback.
